comments.text:
The simulation inside a simulation with simulations all the way down so to speak is an interesting thought experiment but the math doesn't really hold up. Back in college I remember one of our computer science teachers talking about a mathematical proof which showed it was impossible for any system to contain all the information about itself. How this applies to computers is that if you have a computer with any amount of data on it it can't also contain the data of it's own existence such as location of every atom that makes it up. This is because if it did then it would also contain a duplicate copy of the data already on it, which would then also contain a copy of the computer and so on to infinity. Thus the computer would need to be capable of holding infinite data. 

This means that it is impossible to simulate the universe on a 1 to 1 scale no matter how advanced our computers get. We will always be forced to run approximations of the universe in our simulations. Thus if we are in a simulation our universe would only be an approximation of the "real universe" just like any simulations we run would be. And at some point the simulation would break down so they couldn't run simulations of their own.
